Region: Northwest Arabia, on the incense-trade routes; the precise site is debated, with the oasis of al-Ula the usual proposal
History: Two Dedans appear in Genesis and must not be merged silently: Dedan son of Raamah (Genesis 10:7) and Dedan son of Jokshan (Genesis 25:3). The Arabian traders of the prophets are Dedan without further distinction in the text. Jeremiah 25:23 names Dedan among the judged nations, Jeremiah 49:8 warns the inhabitants of Dedan to flee and dwell deep, Ezekiel 27:15 and 27:20 have Dedan trading ivory, ebony, and saddlecloths with Tyre, and Ezekiel 38:13 has Sheba and Dedan questioning Gog's spoil.
Culture: Caravan traders of northwest Arabia, dealing in ivory, ebony, and fine cloth.
Religion: Nothing distinct is recorded of Dedanite religion.
BibleConnection: Dedan is the Arabian merchant in Tyre's market, the warned inhabitant of Jeremiah's oracle, and the questioner of Gog's spoil.
KeyScriptures: Genesis 10:7; Genesis 25:3; Jeremiah 25:23; Jeremiah 49:8; Ezekiel 27:15; Ezekiel 27:20; Ezekiel 38:13
